params.body:
## Why

Pointing at a day or a week in a time chart of Inzichten greyed its column, and the figures appeared in a line under the chart. A reader who points at a bar looks at the bar: the line under the plot changed out of sight, so the chart felt as if it had no hover.

## What

The figures of the pointed period now stand in a bubble beside its column, inside the plot (`x-insights.timechart`: Momentum, Garages, and the page of one garage).

- **What it says.** The period on the first line (the date, or the range of the week or month), with "loopt nog" behind it for the running period. Then one line per series the chart draws, in the series' own mark from the chart palette, name left and value right in tabular figures. The values are the ones the server already formats for the reader's locale (the same strings as the table and the line under the chart), so nothing is formatted twice.
- **Where it stands.** Right of the column; left of it near the right edge; above the plot when neither side has room. Under a finger the order turns around: above the column first, because a hand covers what is beside it. It never overlaps the pointed column, never leaves the plot sideways and rises no further than the card. It is absolutely positioned and takes no room, so pointing moves nothing on the page.
- **One bubble on the tab.** Pointing still highlights the period in every chart of the tab (the `ins-day` event), and every chart still writes the figures in its line under the plot. Only the chart under the pointer, the finger or the focus opens a bubble. Seven charts on one axis would otherwise open seven boxes at the same x, each covering part of the chart above or below it (the rows on a garage's page are 56px high), and the eye would no longer know which one it asked for. The band plus the quiet line keeps the comparison across charts readable.
- **Keyboard and touch.** The arrow keys move the period as before and the bubble follows; Escape puts it away, and so does the focus leaving the plot. A tap shows it, a tap anywhere else clears it.
- **Screen readers.** The `aria-live` line in the foot stays as it was; the bubble is `aria-hidden`, so nothing is read twice.
- **One bubble per bar.** No `data-tip` and no `title` on the chart, so the app-wide tooltip and the browser do not answer as well.
- **Look.** A white surface with a hairline and `--ui-shadow-2`, the `surface` corner, text in the `label` and `note` roles: part of the chart, not the dark tooltip.
- **The hint.** "Wijs een dag aan voor de cijfers" became "Wijs een dag aan en de cijfers staan erbij" (day, week and month; nl, fr, en, de). "Cijfers als tabel" is unchanged.

The chart's Alpine state moved from an inline `x-data` object to `resources/js/insights-timechart.js` (registered as `insTimechart` on `alpine:init`, no new global), so the placement is a pure function that vitest can pin.

## Rule

R P2-10.39 (how a tab of Inzichten is built) now says where the figures of the pointed period stand.

## Tests

- `TheFiguresStandAtTheBarTest` (`@rule P2-10.39`): one bubble per chart, `aria-hidden`, inside the plot; the period, the running mark and a line per series in its own mark; no `data-tip` or `title` anywhere on the chart; the bubble floats and is drawn from the tokens; the hint in four languages.
- `resources/js/insights-timechart.test.js`: right of the column, the flip near the right edge, never over the column and never outside the plot for every column with mouse and touch, above the plot when no side fits, above the column under a finger, clamped to the card; only the pointed chart opens the bubble while every chart follows the period; arrow keys, Escape and a tap elsewhere.

Checked in a browser on local demo data at 1440 (mouse and keyboard) and at 390 (touch): every chart on Momentum, the months chart on Garages and the weekly rows on a garage's page. In each case one open bubble, no app-wide tooltip, the bubble inside its card and clear of the pointed column, no sideways scroll.
params.title: Chart hover shows the figures at the bar
